newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa mostly ends softer amid thin trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa mostly ends softer amid thin trade.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed mostly lower amid sluggish trade on Wednesday.
July slipped three stg to 997 stg per tonne, falling just a stg below Tuesday's low to reach a one-week low. September lost two stg to 1,015.
But trading was thin with total turnover at just 2,848 contracts.
Traders said light sales from French firms in the forward months dominated the lackluster activity. They speculated those sales were Ivory Coast hedges.

Sterling's surge against other major currencies also weighed on London cocoa, some traders said. The UK unit jumped on Wednesday more than two pfennigs against the mark and about a cent against the dollar to near 2.79 marks and just below $1.64, respectively, after a larger-than-expected drop in UK unemployment.
UK unemployment fell 59,000 in April versus forecasts for a 40,000 decline.
But cocoa's losses were buffered by light scaled-down industry buying, which helped keep prices locked in a tight range, traders said.
July/December switches also traded at 13 stg earlier in the day, traders said.

Ivory Coast Commodity Minister Guy-Alain Gauze told Reuters in Singapore on Wednesday afternoon that Ivory Coast production should be between 900,000 and 950,000 tonnes in the October-September 1996/97 season. He added cocoa exports would be about 750,000 to 800,000 tonnes with the rest going to local consumption.

But traders said those remarks did little to spur cocoa out of its recent trading range. The Ivory Coast production forecast has remained the same despite analysts' expectations of more than a million tonnes this year, they said.
Technically, July was still trapped in a range but would likely drift lower to test the bottom end near the April 9 low of 980.
London cocoa shrugged off early gains made in New York as CSCE cocoa retraces some of its recent losses.
In options, no July contracts traded.
